title: Upgrade from Java 11 to Java 17 (Groovy 3.0.19 / Spock 2.3)
body:
## Proposed changes

Upgrades the project from Java 11 to Java 17, including the Groovy/Spock test toolchain and the test-compilation build setup.

**pom.xml (parent)**
- `java.version` `11` → `17` (drives `source`/`target`/`release` via existing property refs)
- Groovy `2.4.21` → `3.0.19`, Spock `1.1-groovy-2.4` → `2.3-groovy-3.0` (extracted to `${groovy.version}` / `${spock.version}` properties)
- Replaced the `groovy-eclipse-compiler` / `groovy-eclipse-batch` joint-compilation setup with `gmavenplus-plugin` `3.0.2`.

  Why: the Groovy 3.x `groovy-eclipse-batch` (last release `3.0.8-01`) embeds an Eclipse JDT compiler that only accepts source levels up to `15` — building with `source/target 17` fails with `source level should be in '1.1'...'1.8','9'...'15': 17`. There is no Groovy-3-compatible eclipse-batch that supports Java 17. GMavenPlus uses the real Groovy 3.0.19 compiler, which supports Java 17 bytecode. `maven-compiler-plugin` (plain `javac`) compiles the Java sources; `gmavenplus:addTestSources` + `gmavenplus:compileTests` compile the Groovy/Spock specs (and pick up the lone `.java` helper in `envvars-yaml/src/test/groovy`, which `javac` compiles first since the compiler plugin is declared earlier).

**envvars-json / envvars-yaml pom.xml**
- Removed the per-module `maven-antrun-plugin` `groovyc` joint-compilation blocks (and the `envvars-yaml` `testSourceDirectory` override). Groovy test compilation is now handled uniformly by the parent's GMavenPlus config.

**.github/workflows/maven-ci.yml**
- `PRIMARY_JAVA_VERSION` `11` → `17`
- Build matrix is now `java: ['17']`. Java 11 was dropped rather than kept "for backward compatibility": with `release 17`, JDK 11 cannot compile the project (and 17 bytecode cannot run on 11), so a Java 11 matrix entry would always fail CI.

Dependency compatibility verified by a full `./mvnw clean install`: `templ-lib 1.1.1`, Jackson `2.17.0`, SnakeYAML `2.2`, and all Maven plugins build and pass on Java 17 — no version bumps required for those.

### Verification
- `./mvnw clean install -D ci.build` → BUILD SUCCESS on Temurin/OpenJDK 17.0.13.
- Tests: `envvars-lib` 97, `envvars-yaml` 17, all passing (json/cli have no tests).
- CLI smoke test against the assembled fat jar resolved injected vars from a YAML file end-to-end:
  ```
  java -jar envvars-cli/target/envvars-jar-with-dependencies.jar \
    '{"applications":"myapp"}' '[{"context":"applications"}]' smoke.yaml
  # -> HOST==HOST / URL==URL
  ```

## Types of changes

- [ ] Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [x] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Documentation only

Breaking: the artifacts now require a Java 17 (or newer) runtime.

## Checklist

- [x] I have read the [CONTRIBUTING](https://github.com/Optum/oss-template/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) doc
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [x] I have added necessary documentation (if appropriate)
- [x] Any dependent changes have been merged and published in downstream modules

No code/test changes were needed — the existing Spock specs compile and pass under Groovy 3.0.19 / Spock 2.3. No docs referenced a specific Java version (README/CONTRIBUTING only say "Java").

## Further comments

The migration from `groovy-eclipse-compiler` to GMavenPlus is the key non-obvious decision; it was required because the Groovy-3 eclipse-batch compiler hard-caps source level at 15. GMavenPlus is the standard, actively-maintained way to compile Groovy/Spock on modern JDKs. Sticking with Groovy 3.0.19 (rather than 4.x) keeps the `org.codehaus.groovy` package coordinates and avoids a larger migration.

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/7372dba5dc0a4bc4b3d2ace9e4f6464a
Requested by: @jennareddell
